library(tidyverse)

statcast_raw <- read_csv("statcast_2025.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

statcast_bip <- statcast_raw |>
  filter(type == "X", !is.na(launch_speed), !is.na(launch_angle), !is.na(events)) |>
  mutate(
    player_id = case_when(
      batter == 669065 ~ "stowers",
      batter == 668939 ~ "rutschman",
      batter == 592450 ~ "judge",
      batter == 677951 ~ "witt"
    ),
    outcome = case_when(
      events == "home_run" ~ "Home Run",
      events %in% c("double", "triple") ~ "Extra-Base Hit (2B/3B)",
      events == "single" ~ "Single",
      TRUE ~ "In-Play Out"
    ),
    outcome = factor(
      outcome,
      levels = c("Home Run", "Extra-Base Hit (2B/3B)", "Single", "In-Play Out")
    ),
    pitch_cat = case_when(
      pitch_type %in% c("FF", "SI", "FC") ~ "Fastballs",
      pitch_type %in% c("SL", "ST", "CU", "KC", "SV", "CS") ~ "Breaking Balls",
      pitch_type %in% c("CH", "FS", "FO") ~ "Offspeed",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    pitch_cat = factor(pitch_cat, levels = c("Fastballs", "Breaking Balls", "Offspeed"))
  )

outcome_colors <- c(
  "Home Run" = "#e63946",
  "Extra-Base Hit (2B/3B)" = "#f4a261",
  "Single" = "#2a9d8f",
  "In-Play Out" = "#adb5bd"
)
```

## ⚾ Introduction

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

make_pitch_plot <- function(data, category_name, sub_text) {
  p_data <- data |> filter(pitch_cat == category_name)
  n_bip <- nrow(p_data)
  n_hr <- sum(p_data$outcome == "Home Run")
  
  p <- ggplot(p_data, aes(x = attack_angle, y = launch_angle, color = outcome)) +
    annotate(
      "rect",
      xmin = 8, xmax = 18, ymin = 20, ymax = 38,
      fill = "#e63946", alpha = 0.12, color = "#e63946", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    annotate(
      "label",
      x = 13, y = 29,
      label = "Optimal Barrel Window\n(8°–18° Attack Angle)",
      size = 3.0, fontface = "bold", color = "#1d3557", fill = "#f1faee"
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(10, 25), linetype = "dotted", color = "gray55") +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.72, size = 2.1) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#1d3557", linewidth = 0.95) +
    scale_color_manual(values = outcome_colors) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-15, 30), breaks = seq(-10, 30, by = 10), labels = \(x) paste0(x, "°")) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-40, 70), breaks = seq(-30, 60, by = 30), labels = \(x) paste0(x, "°")) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Bat Swing Path on ", category_name, " (", n_bip, " Balls in Play, ", n_hr, " Home Runs)"),
      subtitle = sub_text,
      x = "Bat Swing Path Attack Angle (degrees)",
      y = "Batted-Ball Launch Angle (degrees)",
      color = "Batted-Ball Outcome",
      caption = "Data: 2025 MLB Statcast via Baseball Savant | Hawk-Eye Bat Tracking"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13.5, color = "#1d3557"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", size = 10, margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.caption = element_text(color = "gray45", size = 8.5, margin = margin(t = 6)),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1d3557", size = 10.5),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1d3557", size = 9.5),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray85", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8)
    )
  
  tf <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  ggsave(tf, p, width = 8.5, height = 4.8, dpi = 130)
  knitr::image_uri(tf)
}

clean_bip <- statcast_bip |>
  filter(!is.na(attack_angle), !is.na(launch_angle), !is.na(pitch_cat), pitch_cat != "Other") |>
  filter(attack_angle >= -15, attack_angle <= 30, launch_angle >= -40, launch_angle <= 70)

uri_fast <- make_pitch_plot(clean_bip, "Fastballs", "High incoming velocity meets bat path: tightest launch angle clustering and highest home run ceiling.")
uri_break <- make_pitch_plot(clean_bip, "Breaking Balls", "Downward break disrupts attack angle alignment: induces more miss-hits and off-barrel contact.")
uri_off <- make_pitch_plot(clean_bip, "Offspeed", "Deceptive deceleration challenges timing: batters swing out in front, flattening their path.")

html_out <- paste0(
'<div class="pitch-anim-container">
<div class="pitch-anim-header">
<div class="pitch-anim-badge">
<span class="pitch-anim-pulsing-dot"></span>
<span>Live Pitch Type Cycle: <strong id="pitch-active-label" style="color: #e63946;">Fastballs</strong></span>
</div>
<div class="pitch-anim-pills">
<button class="pitch-pill active" id="pill-0" onclick="selectPitchSlide(0)">Fastballs</button>
<button class="pitch-pill" id="pill-1" onclick="selectPitchSlide(1)">Breaking Balls</button>
<button class="pitch-pill" id="pill-2" onclick="selectPitchSlide(2)">Offspeed</button>
</div>
</div>
<div class="pitch-anim-stage">
<div class="pitch-slide active" id="pitch-slide-0">
<img src="', uri_fast, '" alt="Bat Swing Path on Fastballs" />
</div>
<div class="pitch-slide" id="pitch-slide-1">
<img src="', uri_break, '" alt="Bat Swing Path on Breaking Balls" />
</div>
<div class="pitch-slide" id="pitch-slide-2">
<img src="', uri_off, '" alt="Bat Swing Path on Offspeed Pitches" />
</div>
</div>
<div class="pitch-progress-track">
<div class="pitch-progress-bar" id="pitch-progress-fill"></div>
</div>
<div class="pitch-anim-caption">
<span>Data automatically cycles pitch types every 6 seconds. Click any button above to pause on a specific pitch type.</span>
<span><strong>Statcast 2025</strong></span>
</div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {
var currentPitchIdx = 0;
var totalPitchSlides = 3;
var slideIntervalMs = 6000;
var pitchTimerId = null;
var progressTimerId = null;
var progressStart = Date.now();

function updatePitchSlide(index) {
currentPitchIdx = index;
var slides = [document.getElementById("pitch-slide-0"), document.getElementById("pitch-slide-1"), document.getElementById("pitch-slide-2")];
var pills = [document.getElementById("pill-0"), document.getElementById("pill-1"), document.getElementById("pill-2")];
var label = document.getElementById("pitch-active-label");
var names = ["Fastballs", "Breaking Balls", "Offspeed"];

for (var i = 0; i < totalPitchSlides; i++) {
if (slides[i]) slides[i].classList.toggle("active", i === index);
if (pills[i]) pills[i].classList.toggle("active", i === index);
}
if (label) label.textContent = names[index];
progressStart = Date.now();
}

function nextPitchSlide() {
updatePitchSlide((currentPitchIdx + 1) % totalPitchSlides);
}

function startCycle() {
if (pitchTimerId) clearInterval(pitchTimerId);
if (progressTimerId) clearInterval(progressTimerId);

progressStart = Date.now();
pitchTimerId = setInterval(nextPitchSlide, slideIntervalMs);

progressTimerId = setInterval(function() {
var elapsed = Date.now() - progressStart;
var pct = Math.min(100, (elapsed / slideIntervalMs) * 100);
var bar = document.getElementById("pitch-progress-fill");
if (bar) bar.style.width = pct + "%";
}, 60);
}

window.selectPitchSlide = function(index) {
updatePitchSlide(index);
startCycle();
};

if (document.readyState === "complete" || document.readyState === "interactive") {
startCycle();
} else {
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", startCycle);
}
})();
</script>'
)

cat(knitr::raw_html(html_out))
```

Modern Major League Baseball analytics has been revolutionized by Hawk-Eye optical tracking and bat-sensor Statcast data provided through **Baseball Savant**. While traditional metrics focused solely on pitch velocity and movement, newly available swing-tracking technology captures the 3D trajectory of the bat barrel through the hitting zone. **This project is specifically focused on how a hitter's bat swing path—in particular, their vertical attack angle and swing plane through the zone—shapes contact quality and dictates batted-ball outcomes.**

A hitter's swing path is the fundamental blueprint for ball flight. A swing path that is too steep or too flat frequently leads to rolled-over ground balls or weak pop-ups. Conversely, an optimized bat path that closely mirrors the downward approach angle of incoming pitches creates a wider window of square contact, driving balls into the line-drive and high-value "barrel" zones. In this project, I examine how bat swing path metrics interact with pitch characteristics to produce outs, singles, extra-base hits, and home runs across elite MLB batters.

::: {.callout-important}
### Core Research Question
How does a hitter's **bat swing path** (specifically their vertical attack angle) interact with pitch type to shape **launch angle** and **exit velocity**, and what swing paths consistently maximize extra-base hits and home runs?
:::

## 📊 Data & Variables

The data for this analysis comes from **MLB Statcast** via Baseball Savant, where each observation represents an individual pitch put into play. Below is a summary of the core variables I use to model and explain swing outcomes:

| Variable | Statcast Column | Units / Categories | Role in Analysis |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Attack Angle (Bat Path)** | `attack_angle` | Degrees ($-15^\circ\text{ to }30^\circ$) | Vertical path of the bat barrel at contact |
| **Exit Velocity** | `launch_speed` | mph ($60\text{--}118\text{ mph}$) | Measures raw contact hardness off the bat |
| **Launch Angle** | `launch_angle` | Degrees ($-45^\circ\text{ to }75^\circ$) | Determines trajectory (grounder, liner, fly ball) |
| **Bat Speed** | `bat_speed` | mph ($60\text{--}85\text{ mph}$) | Captures batter swing effort at the sweet spot |
| **Pitch Type** | `pitch_type` | Fastball, Slider, Changeup, Curveball | Accounts for movement profile and deception |
| **Release Velocity** | `release_speed` | mph ($75\text{--}102\text{ mph}$) | Measures incoming pitch speed out of the hand |

::: {.stat-card}
**Why These Variables Matter Together:**

- **Bat Path Attack Angle (`attack_angle`):** Dictates how cleanly the barrel plane matches the downward flight of the pitch. An upward path of $8^\circ\text{--}18^\circ$ maximizes line-drive and extra-base hit launch angles.
- **Exit Velocity (`launch_speed`) & Launch Angle (`launch_angle`):** Higher exit velocities give fielders less time to react and carry the ball farther, but hard contact hit straight into the ground ($< 5^\circ$) often results in an out. Pairing $98+\text{ mph}$ exit velocity with an optimal launch angle ($24^\circ\text{--}38^\circ$) defines the **Barrel Zone**, where home runs are most frequent.
- **Bat Speed (`bat_speed`):** Introduced in recent Statcast tracking, bat speed separates a batter's raw swing effort from point-of-contact quality.
- **Pitch Type (`pitch_type`) & Release Velocity (`release_speed`):** Fastballs provide incoming kinetic energy that can boost exit velocity when squared up, whereas breaking and offspeed pitches disrupt timing and induce weaker launch angles.
:::

:::

::: {.stat-card}
### Key Insights from the League-Wide Batted-Ball Distribution

- **The Power of the Barrel Zone ($24^\circ\text{--}38^\circ$, $98+\text{ mph}$):** Notice the tight cluster of red **Home Runs** concentrated inside the shaded rectangle. Balls struck with both elite exit velocity and an optimal launch angle produce an expected slugging percentage near $2.000$, resulting in nearly all home run production in the 2025 dataset.
- **Line Drives Drive Batting Average ($10^\circ\text{--}25^\circ$):** The teal points (**Singles**) and orange points (**Extra-Base Hits**) dominate this corridor. Line drives regularly travel over the heads of the infielders while landing in the gaps ahead of outfielders, maximizing on-base probability.
- **The Ground Ball Trap ($< 10^\circ$):** Even when a batter makes blisteringly hard contact ($100+\text{ mph}$) into the ground, turf friction and infielder positioning limit the outcome to in-play outs or routine singles. Downward contact almost never produces extra bases.
- **Pop-Ups and Ineffective Lift ($> 50^\circ$):** Regardless of how hard the ball is struck, balls launched at extreme upward angles hang in the air for 5+ seconds, allowing fielders to settle underneath them for routine outs ($> 98\%$ out rate).
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Takeaway for Batter Approach
Maximizing offensive production is not simply a matter of hitting the ball hard—it requires directing kinetic energy into the **$10^\circ\text{ to }35^\circ$ launch window** where ball flight physics and field dimensions yield the greatest offensive run expectancy.
:::

## 📖 Swing Story

When Baseball Savant added Hawk-Eye bat tracking to Statcast, it revealed a swing mechanic that traditional box-score stats could never see: **Attack Angle** (`attack_angle`), the vertical direction in degrees that the bat's sweet spot is traveling at the exact moment it meets the baseball (`0°` is perfectly level with the ground, positive angles move upward, and negative angles chop downward). Across the **1,405 tracked balls in play** in our 2025 Statcast dataset featuring Aaron Judge, Bobby Witt Jr., Kyle Stowers, and Adley Rutschman, plotting every swing's attack angle against its resulting exit velocity and batted-ball outcome exposes a clear offensive "Goldilocks" zone.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 5.4

story_aa <- statcast_bip |>
  filter(!is.na(attack_angle))

ggplot(story_aa, aes(x = attack_angle, y = launch_speed, color = outcome)) +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 10, xmax = 20, ymin = 55, ymax = 120,
    fill = "#e63946", alpha = 0.10, color = "#e63946", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = 15, y = 116,
    label = "OPTIMAL ATTACK WINDOW (10°–20°)\n94.5 mph Avg EV • 16%–18% Barrels • .531–.575 wOBA",
    size = 2.9, fontface = "bold", color = "#1d3557", fill = "#f1faee", label.size = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", color = "gray55", linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = -8.5, y = 58, label = "Downward Chop (< 0°)\n0.9% HR • Grounders", color = "gray40", size = 2.9, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 26.5, y = 58, label = "Too Steep (> 20°)\n85.5 mph EV • Pop-Ups", color = "gray40", size = 2.9, fontface = "italic") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.72, size = 2.0) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(group = 1),
    method = "loess", se = FALSE, span = 0.65,
    color = "#1d3557", linewidth = 1.15
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(5.2, 11.0), linetype = "dotdash", color = "#1d3557", alpha = 0.55) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.7, y = 109.5, label = "Witt Jr. Avg (5.2°)", hjust = 1, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", color = "#1d3557") +
  annotate("text", x = 11.4, y = 109.5, label = "Judge Avg (11.0°)", hjust = 0, size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", color = "#1d3557") +
  scale_color_manual(values = outcome_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-15, 30, by = 5), labels = \(x) paste0(x, "°")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(60, 115, by = 10), labels = \(x) paste0(x, " mph")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-15, 32), ylim = c(55, 120)) +
  labs(
    title = "The 10°–20° Sweet Spot: Swing Attack Angle vs. Exit Velocity & Outcome",
    subtitle = "Solid navy curve tracks rolling average Exit Velocity; home runs and barrels surge inside the 10°–20° upward window",
    x = "Bat Attack Angle at Impact (degrees)",
    y = "Exit Velocity (mph)",
    color = "Swing Outcome",
    caption = paste0("Source: Baseball Savant 2025 Statcast CSV export (n = ", nrow(story_aa), " tracked balls in play)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13.5, color = "#1d3557"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", size = 10, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "gray45", size = 8.5, margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1d3557"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1d3557"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

The static chart above shows that **swings meeting the ball on a `10°` to `20°` upward path generate by far the most destructive contact in baseball**. Inside the `10°–15°` and `15°–20°` bands, average exit velocity peaks at **`94.5 mph`**, barrel rates climb to **`15.6%–17.7%`**, extra-base hits jump to **`22.2%–24.0%`**, and hitters post a massive **`.531` to `.575` wOBA** on balls in play (`11.4%–14.6%` home runs). Outside that window, production falls off in two completely different ways: downward chops below `0°` beat the ball into the turf (`1.9°` average launch angle), yielding `32.6%` singles but an almost nonexistent **`0.9%` home run rate**, whereas overly steep uppercuts above `20°` slice underneath the baseball—causing average exit velocity to plunge nearly 9 mph to **`85.5 mph`** and barrels to collapse from `17.7%` down to **`5.7%`**.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 3.1

# Supplemental fixed context diagram: why 10°–20° matches the incoming pitch plane
pitch_line <- tibble(x = c(18, -14), y = c(3.2, -1.6)) # ~8.5° downward pitch descent

plane_df <- tibble(
  x0 = c(-4, -4, -4),
  y0 = c(0.2, -0.5, -1.2),
  ang = c(-5, 14, 26),
  label = c("Downward Chop (-5°): Grounders", "On-Plane Sweet Spot (+14°): Barrels", "Steep Uppercut (+26°): Pop-Ups"),
  col = c("#2a9d8f", "#e63946", "#adb5bd")
) |>
  mutate(
    rad = ang * pi / 180,
    x1 = x0 + 13 * cos(rad),
    y1 = y0 + 13 * sin(rad)
  )

ggplot() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -16, xmax = 20, ymin = -4.2, ymax = 5.8, fill = "#f8f9fa", color = "gray80") +
  annotate("polygon", x = c(-3.5, 3.5, 2.4, -2.4), y = c(-3.4, -3.4, -3.9, -3.9), fill = "white", color = "#1d3557", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = -2.85, label = "HOME PLATE (SIDE VIEW)", size = 2.6, fontface = "bold", color = "#1d3557") +
  geom_line(data = pitch_line, aes(x, y), color = "#1d3557", linewidth = 1.2, linetype = "dashed",
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.22, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
  annotate("text", x = 12.5, y = 3.35, label = "Incoming Pitch Plane (~6° to 10° downward)", size = 3.0, fontface = "bold", color = "#1d3557") +
  geom_segment(
    data = plane_df,
    aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1, color = col),
    linewidth = 1.6, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.22, "cm"), type = "closed")
  ) +
  annotate("point", x = -1.2, y = 0.3, size = 4.2, shape = 21, fill = "#ffb703", color = "#1d3557", stroke = 1.0) +
  annotate("text", x = 9.8, y = -0.95, label = "Chop (< 0°): Cuts across ball → topspin grounder", hjust = 0, size = 2.85, fontface = "bold", color = "#2a9d8f") +
  annotate("text", x = 9.2, y = 2.25, label = "Optimal (+10° to +20°): Matches pitch plane → flush carry", hjust = 0, size = 2.95, fontface = "bold", color = "#e63946") +
  annotate("text", x = 5.5, y = 4.85, label = "Steep (> 20°): Clips bottom of ball → glancing pop-up", hjust = 0, size = 2.85, fontface = "bold", color = "gray40") +
  scale_color_identity() +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(-16, 28), ylim = c(-4.3, 5.9), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Why 10°–20° Works: Matching the Downward Plane of an MLB Pitch",
    subtitle = "Because pitches descend across the plate at 6°–10°, a 10°–20° upward barrel path stays flush with the ball longest"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12.5, color = "#1d3557", margin = margin(b = 3)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "gray35", margin = margin(b = 6))
  )
```

The physics diagram above puts this sweet spot into context: because a pitcher releases the baseball from an elevated mound, nearly every fastball and breaking ball crosses home plate moving **downward at `6°` to `10°`**. A hitter whose barrel rises at **`10°` to `20°`** meets that descending pitch nearly head-on, keeping the sweet spot aligned with the ball's path across a wider timing window instead of grazing it at a single point. That explains the distinct player archetypes in our dataset: power hitters **Aaron Judge (`11.0°` average attack angle, `.583` wOBA)** and **Kyle Stowers (`10.0°`, `.518` wOBA)** live right at the front door of the `10°–20°` damage zone, while **Bobby Witt Jr. (`5.2°`, `.422` wOBA)** intentionally trades loft (`4.6%` home runs per ball in play) for a flatter line-drive stroke that lets his elite bat speed (`74.6 mph`) and sprint speed turn hard grounders and low liners into extra bases.

## 🔍 Player Exploration

Use the dropdown menu below to inspect real **2025 Statcast swing outcomes** exported from Baseball Savant for four featured hitters: **Kyle Stowers**, **Adley Rutschman**, **Aaron Judge**, and **Bobby Witt Jr.**

```{r}
player_notes <- c(
  stowers = "Power-oriented left-handed swing (74.9 mph avg bat speed, 25 HRs in 2025) with strong pull-side barrel production.",
  rutschman = "Switch-hitting catcher (69.8 mph avg bat speed, 6.9 ft compact swing length) with consistent line-drive contact.",
  judge = "Generational Statcast outlier combining 76.1 mph average bat speed with 95.1 mph average exit velocity and 55 home runs.",
  witt = "Explosive 74.6 mph bat speed paired with a flat 5° attack angle that produces 543 balls in play and 26 home runs."
)

players_2025 <- statcast_bip |>
  mutate(
    game_date = as.Date(game_date),
    bat_speed = coalesce(bat_speed, median(bat_speed, na.rm = TRUE)),
    profile_note = unname(player_notes[player_id])
  )

plot_player_2025 <- \(df, p_name) {
  ggplot(df, aes(x = game_date, y = launch_speed, color = outcome)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 95, linetype = "dashed", color = "#1d3557", alpha = 0.5) +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = min(df$game_date, na.rm = TRUE) + 5, y = 96.8,
      label = "Hard-Hit Threshold (95 mph)",
      hjust = 0, size = 3, fontface = "italic", color = "#1d3557"
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(size = bat_speed), alpha = 0.82) +
    geom_smooth(
      aes(group = 1),
      method = "loess", se = FALSE,
      color = "#1d3557", linewidth = 0.9, linetype = "solid"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = outcome_colors, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.6, 3.8), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b 2025") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(55, 120), breaks = seq(65, 115, by = 10), labels = \(x) paste0(x, " mph")) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(p_name, " — 2025 Batted-Ball Outcomes Across the Season (n = ", nrow(df), " BIP)"),
      subtitle = "Each point is a real 2025 ball in play (sized by Bat Speed); solid navy trend line tracks rolling Exit Velocity",
      x = "2025 Season Date",
      y = "Exit Velocity (mph)",
      color = "Swing Outcome",
      caption = "Source: Baseball Savant 2025 Statcast CSV export"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13.5, color = "#1d3557"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray30", size = 10),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1d3557"),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#1d3557"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
}

render_savant_swing_video <- \(p_id) {
  cfg <- list(
    stowers   = list(mlb_id = 669065, side = "L", switch = FALSE, preload = "auto"),
    rutschman = list(mlb_id = 668939, side = "L", switch = TRUE,  preload = "metadata"),
    judge     = list(mlb_id = 592450, side = "R", switch = FALSE, preload = "metadata"),
    witt      = list(mlb_id = 677951, side = "R", switch = FALSE, preload = "metadata")
  )[[p_id]]

  base_url <- "https://builds.mlbstatic.com/baseballsavant.mlb.com/swing-path/splendid-splinter"
  mp4_url  <- sprintf("%s/cut/%d-2025-%s.mp4", base_url, cfg$mlb_id, cfg$side)
  png_url  <- sprintf("%s/posterized/%d-2025-%s.png", base_url, cfg$mlb_id, cfg$side)

  side_btns <- if (cfg$switch) {
    sprintf(
      '<button type="button" id="side-L-%s" class="savant-btn active-side" onclick="setSavantSide(\'%s\', %d, \'L\')">LHB</button><button type="button" id="side-R-%s" class="savant-btn" onclick="setSavantSide(\'%s\', %d, \'R\')">RHB</button>',
      p_id, p_id, cfg$mlb_id, p_id, p_id, cfg$mlb_id
    )
  } else {
    ""
  }

  cat(sprintf('\n```{=html}\n<div class="savant-viz-wrapper">
  <div class="savant-video-stage" onclick="toggleSavantVideo(\'%s\', event)">
    <video id="savant-vid-%s" muted playsinline loop preload="%s" poster="%s">
      <source id="savant-src-%s" src="%s" type="video/mp4">
    </video>
    <div class="savant-right-hotspots">
      <div class="savant-hotspot" title="Jump to Attack Angle breakdown" onclick="jumpSavantMetric(\'%s\', 10.0, event)"></div>
      <div class="savant-hotspot" title="Jump to Attack Direction breakdown" onclick="jumpSavantMetric(\'%s\', 12.3, event)"></div>
      <div class="savant-hotspot" title="Jump to Swing Path Tilt breakdown" onclick="jumpSavantMetric(\'%s\', 16.88, event)"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="savant-controls-bar">
    <div class="savant-btn-group">
      <button type="button" id="play-btn-%s" class="savant-btn" onclick="toggleSavantVideo(\'%s\', event)">▶ Play</button>
      <button type="button" class="savant-btn" onclick="replaySavantVideo(\'%s\')">⏪ Replay</button>
      %s
    </div>
    <input type="range" id="scrub-%s" class="savant-scrub" min="0" max="1000" value="0" oninput="scrubSavantVideo(\'%s\', this.value)">
    <div class="savant-btn-group">
      <button type="button" class="savant-btn" onclick="jumpSavantMetric(\'%s\', 10.0, event)">Attack Angle</button>
      <button type="button" class="savant-btn" onclick="jumpSavantMetric(\'%s\', 12.3, event)">Attack Dir</button>
      <button type="button" class="savant-btn" onclick="jumpSavantMetric(\'%s\', 16.88, event)">Swing Tilt</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>\n```\n',
    p_id, p_id, cfg$preload, png_url, p_id, mp4_url,
    p_id, p_id, p_id,
    p_id, p_id, p_id, side_btns,
    p_id, p_id,
    p_id, p_id, p_id
  ))
}
```

- **Bat Path & Attack Angle:** Features an **Attack Angle** of **$10^\circ$** ($10.0^\circ$ on BIP, $10.6^\circ$ overall), an **Attack Direction** of **$+2.0^\circ$** (pull side), and a **Swing Path Tilt** of **$34.2^\circ$**. With a compact **Swing Length** of **$6.7\text{ ft}$** ($6.63\text{ ft}$ overall) and **$74.9\text{ mph}$** avg bat speed on contact ($73.0\text{ mph}$ overall, $25$ HRs), he matches the downward pitch plane flush to generate strong pull-side barrels and extra-base power.

```{=html}
<script>
const teamBannerColors = {
  stowers: "linear-gradient(135deg, #00A3E0 0%, #0077a8 100%)",
  rutschman: "linear-gradient(135deg, #DF4601 0%, #000000 100%)",
  judge: "linear-gradient(135deg, #0C2340 0%, #1f3a60 100%)",
  witt: "linear-gradient(135deg, #004687 0%, #BD9B60 100%)"
};

function syncPlayBtn(pId) {
  const vid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + pId);
  const btn = document.getElementById('play-btn-' + pId);
  if (vid && btn) {
    btn.textContent = vid.paused ? '▶ Play' : '⏸ Pause';
  }
}

function toggleSavantVideo(pId, evt) {
  if (evt) evt.stopPropagation();
  const vid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + pId);
  if (!vid) return;
  if (vid.paused) {
    vid.play();
  } else {
    vid.pause();
  }
  syncPlayBtn(pId);
}

function replaySavantVideo(pId) {
  const vid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + pId);
  if (!vid) return;
  vid.currentTime = 0;
  vid.play();
  syncPlayBtn(pId);
}

function jumpSavantMetric(pId, sec, evt) {
  if (evt) evt.stopPropagation();
  const vid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + pId);
  if (!vid) return;
  vid.pause();
  vid.currentTime = sec;
  syncPlayBtn(pId);
}

function scrubSavantVideo(pId, val) {
  const vid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + pId);
  if (!vid || !vid.duration) return;
  vid.pause();
  vid.currentTime = (Number(val) / 1000) * vid.duration;
  syncPlayBtn(pId);
}

function setSavantSide(pId, mlbId, side) {
  const vid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + pId);
  const src = document.getElementById('savant-src-' + pId);
  if (!vid || !src) return;
  const base = 'https://builds.mlbstatic.com/baseballsavant.mlb.com/swing-path/splendid-splinter';
  vid.poster = `${base}/posterized/${mlbId}-2025-${side}.png`;
  src.src = `${base}/cut/${mlbId}-2025-${side}.mp4`;
  document.getElementById('side-L-' + pId)?.classList.toggle('active-side', side === 'L');
  document.getElementById('side-R-' + pId)?.classList.toggle('active-side', side === 'R');
  vid.load();
  vid.play();
  syncPlayBtn(pId);
}

['stowers', 'rutschman', 'judge', 'witt'].forEach(pId => {
  const vid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + pId);
  const scrub = document.getElementById('scrub-' + pId);
  if (vid) {
    vid.addEventListener('timeupdate', () => {
      if (scrub && vid.duration) {
        scrub.value = Math.round((vid.currentTime / vid.duration) * 1000);
      }
    });
    vid.addEventListener('play', () => syncPlayBtn(pId));
    vid.addEventListener('pause', () => syncPlayBtn(pId));
  }
});

function switchPlayer(playerId) {
  const panels = document.querySelectorAll('.player-panel');
  panels.forEach(p => p.classList.remove('active-player'));
  document.querySelectorAll('.savant-video-stage video').forEach(v => v.pause());
  const target = document.getElementById('panel-' + playerId);
  if (target) {
    target.classList.add('active-player');
  }
  const activeVid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + playerId);
  if (activeVid) {
    activeVid.currentTime = 0;
    activeVid.play().catch(() => {});
  }
  const bar = document.getElementById('selector-bar');
  if (bar && teamBannerColors[playerId]) {
    bar.style.background = teamBannerColors[playerId];
  }
}

document.addEventListener('shown.bs.tab', evt => {
  if (evt.target && evt.target.textContent.includes('Exploration')) {
    const sel = document.getElementById('player-select');
    const activeVid = document.getElementById('savant-vid-' + (sel ? sel.value : 'stowers'));
    if (activeVid && activeVid.paused) {
      activeVid.play().catch(() => {});
    }
  } else {
    document.querySelectorAll('.savant-video-stage video').forEach(v => v.pause());
  }
});
</script>
```

### Data Source

All pitch-level and bat-tracking data used in this project come from Major League Baseball's Hawk-Eye optical tracking system via [Baseball Savant](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/). Specifically, the 2025 pitch-by-pitch batted-ball dataset (`statcast_2025.csv`) was exported using [Statcast Search](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_search), and the animated 3D swing-path and attack-angle visuals are sourced from Baseball Savant's [Bat Tracking Swing Path & Attack Angle Leaderboard](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/leaderboard/bat-tracking/swing-path-attack-angle).
:::
